findings.evidence: " | Trunk-based | GitFlow" ... "Needs fast automated tests on every commit" / "Broken trunk: fix or revert first, before anything else"
findings.fix: Add a header such as 'Aspect' to the table, and move the two lines into a short 'Rules' list under their own heading.

findings.summary: The rebase bullet holds two ideas, and the commands are shown before the idea is stated.
findings.evidence: "Rebase before merging: keeps history linear" ... bash block with 'git switch main && git pull'
findings.fix: Split the bullet into 'Rebase onto fresh main' and 'Squash merge keeps trunk linear'. Put the one-line idea above the code block.

findings.summary: The Merging section is headed 'Merging' but its table is about squash merge only. The table header 'Squash merge | Result' mixes a label and a header, and the squash merge command or setting is not shown.
findings.evidence: "Squash merge | Result" / "Trunk history | one commit per change"
findings.fix: Header the table 'Aspect | With squash merge' and state the rule in a bullet: 'Squash merge each PR into trunk'.

findings.summary: The first bullet of The Daily Cycle packs a six-step process into one line of text, and the following bullet does the same for a cycle and a size rule.
findings.evidence: "Cycle: branch from fresh main, commit small, open PR, merge, delete branch same day"
findings.fix: Draw the cycle as a flow diagram (branch → commit → PR → merge → delete) like the other pages' flows.

findings.summary: The 'Why CI Slows Down' flow lists nodes and captions in a single run, so a learner cannot tell which caption belongs to which arrow.
findings.evidence: "feature/* / merges when finished / develop / late integration / release/* / stabilization / main / tag and ship"
findings.fix: Label each arrow explicitly, e.g. feature/* → develop (late integration) → release/* (stabilization) → main (tag and ship).

findings.summary: The Q&A on the interview page is posed with its answer on the same line, so it cannot be self-tested. 'Biggest hotfix risk?' also conflicts with the callout saying one forgotten merge brings the bug back.
findings.evidence: "Why is GitFlow slow? Late merges, many branches to build, a release gate" / "Biggest hotfix risk? Skipping the merge back to develop"
findings.fix: Make the questions visible as prompts with answers set apart. Use the same wording in the hotfix callout ('merge back to develop').

findings.summary: The term "semantic merge conflict" is used without being defined or illustrated, so the learner cannot see what a merge queue protects against.
findings.evidence: "Stops a semantic merge conflict from breaking main"
findings.fix: Add one line defining it: two PRs each pass CI alone and merge textually clean, but together break the build (for example, one renames a function the other calls). The queue catches this by testing each PR on top of the PRs ahead of it.

findings.summary: The merge queue section describes a pipeline as fragments and then adds two unrelated setup bullets.
findings.evidence: "PR queued / Rebuilt on PRs ahead / CI runs / Merge to main" followed by "Enable it in branch protection" / "CI must also trigger on the merge_group event"
findings.fix: Show the queue as a labelled flow (PR queued → rebuilt on top of PRs ahead → CI runs → merge to main) and put the setup steps in a separate 'Setup' list.

findings.summary: The release branch section's first bullet holds two ideas, and the 'Fix on trunk first' rule has no stated reason on this page.
findings.evidence: "release/1.4 is cut from trunk only to support old versions" / "Fix on trunk first, then cherry-pick to the release branch"
findings.fix: Split into 'Cut release/x.y only to support old versions' and 'Fix on trunk first, so later releases keep the fix', then show the cherry-pick command.

findings.summary: The path filter section's bullets mix a rule with its failure reason, and the YAML is shown immediately after a long run of text.
findings.evidence: "Add shared deps: libs/, lockfile, the workflow file itself" / "Else dependents skip tests they need"
findings.fix: Merge the two into one bullet: 'Include shared deps, or dependents skip tests they need', and list the three kinds of shared dep as sub-items.

findings.summary: The required-check deadlock diagram is a list of fragments, so the cause (skipped workflow) and the fix (always-run detect job) are not visibly separate.
findings.evidence: "Detect job / always runs / dorny/paths-filter / what changed? / Gated jobs / only if changed"
findings.fix: Show a two-box flow (Detect job, always runs → Gated jobs, only if changed) next to the problem statement, and label which part is the fix.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet repeats the whole SemVer bump table in reduced form, dropping the 'lower numbers reset' rule from page 4, and mixes commands with rules without separating them.
findings.evidence: "MAJOR | breaking change" (page 6) vs "2.0.0 (lower reset)" (page 4)
findings.fix: Add 'MAJOR resets MINOR and PATCH to 0' to the cheat sheet table.

findings.summary: The self-check page gives each question and its answers in a flat list, so a learner cannot cover the answer before reading it. The second answer also holds two ideas.
findings.evidence: "Trunk never gets the fix, so 1.5 ships with the bug again." / "Fix on trunk first, then git cherry-pick -x <sha> onto the release branch."
findings.fix: Separate each question from a labelled 'Answer:' and split cause and fix into two lines.
